recent_posts.title: WebMCP Is A Free AI In Your App
Partial Page Caching Using React Server Components
recent_posts.summary: A practical demonstration of using React Server Components (RSCs) in TanStack Start to implement partial page caching via a CDN. The approach allows different sections of a page to be cached and invalidated at different rates — for example, static article content cached long-term while a trending sidebar is busted frequently. The key mechanism is a GET-based server function that returns RSC flight data, which the CDN can cache independently from the main page route. An additional benefit shown is code-splitting: interactive client components are only sent to the browser when the RSC payload actually references them, avoiding large monolithic bundles. The author frames RSCs as a specialized tool suited for content sites and widget-heavy dashboards, not a universal architecture requirement.

recent_posts.title: Five ways to handle SSR and RSC in TanStack Start
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of five different data-fetching and rendering strategies available in TanStack Start: client-side rendering (CSR), standard SSR, data-only SSR, RSC via the low-level renderServerComponent API, and RSC via the createCompositeComponent API. Each approach is demonstrated with a Pokémon API example, showing how TanStack Start's route loaders coordinate data fetching across all variants. The post also clarifies that React has supported SSR since its inception, long before Next.js standardized it.

recent_posts.title: Why TanStack Start is not vulnerable to the React2Shell CVE
recent_posts.summary: TanStack Start's new React Server Components support does not expose apps to the React2Shell CVE that affects Next.js. Three key reasons explain why: TanStack Start routes server functions to module-specific URLs (not a predictable slash endpoint), only includes server function code when explicitly defined, and uses the Seroval data format instead of React's flight data format. Flight data's object reference traversal mechanism is the root cause of React2Shell, and Seroval avoids this attack vector entirely. Past CVEs against Seroval were permanently fixed without the single-payload attack surface that flight data has.

recent_posts.title: Introducing TanStack AI Code Mode
recent_posts.summary: TanStack AI Code Mode is a new approach to LLM tool calling that replaces multiple round-trip tool invocations with generated TypeScript code executed in an isolate (QuickJS, Node, or Cloudflare Workers). Instead of 4 LLM round trips and 9.8KB of context for a simple query, Code Mode achieves the same result in 2 calls with 1.7KB of context and 3x faster execution. An additional 'skills' layer lets the LLM persist and reuse generated TypeScript functions, reducing subsequent calls further. The system also supports connecting directly to databases and dynamically generating UI components via code.

recent_posts.title: Netlify.new - AI Builder for TanStack Start Apps!
recent_posts.summary: Netlify has integrated an AI application builder into its platform that generates and deploys TanStack Start applications. Users can choose from AI agents including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Google Gemini, then provide custom prompts or use pre-built templates. A demo shows building a dark-themed AI chat widget for a site, followed by iterative changes via an agent runner — all without writing code manually. The first few builds are free.

recent_posts.title: Generating Images With TanStack AI
recent_posts.summary: TanStack AI supports more than just chatbots — it can generate images, video, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and structured output. A walkthrough shows how to use the `generateImage` function with OpenRouter's adapter to produce AI-generated images. The integration requires importing an adapter (e.g., `openRouterImage`), configuring an adapter config map, and passing a prompt, image count, and size. Results return as an array of objects containing a URL, base64-encoded data, and a revised prompt. OpenRouter is now an officially supported TanStack AI partner and financial sponsor.

recent_posts.title: TanStack Start SSR modes explained with code examples
recent_posts.summary: TanStack Start offers three notable SSR features: SSR is enabled by default with minimal setup, it can be disabled per-route with a single `ssr: false` flag for client-only rendering, and a unique 'data only' mode fetches data server-side but renders exclusively on the client. The data-only mode is especially useful for dashboards, avoiding redundant server and client rendering cycles. Loaders must use server functions to ensure correct execution context, and everything is strongly typed end-to-end.

recent_posts.title: Open Claw + TypeSense Tutorial
recent_posts.summary: A short walkthrough showing how to use Typesense as a document store backend for Open Claw, a web development article search tool. Covers creating a Typesense client, connecting to a server, adding documents individually or in bulk, and performing fast searches with search params.

recent_posts.title: WebMCP is MCP for Single Page Apps!
recent_posts.summary: WebMCP is an emerging standard that enables Single Page Applications to expose tools to AI agents via the Model Context Protocol. Using a Chrome extension called MCP-B as a polyfill, SPAs can register MCP tools (like get_menu, add_to_cart) through a `registerWebMCPTools` function that checks for `navigator.modelContext`. A demo shows a React/Zustand-based food ordering app where an AI agent calls these in-page tools to browse a menu and add items to a cart — without scraping the DOM. MCP-B also exposes an MCP URL that can connect desktop AI clients like Claude directly to the browser extension, enabling a full chain from desktop LLM to live SPA state.
